title: Crossing the Red Sea
place: The Red Sea crossing site: a broad corridor of exposed, rippled wet seabed running from the flat western shore toward the jagged red-brown mountains of the far shore, walled left and right by towering dark blue-green water while the sea is divided.
timeOfDay: One night into the first light of morning: deep night while the sea parts and Israel crosses; pale dawn when the waters return.
weather: A strong, dry east wind all night: driven spray and blown sand, torn low clouds racing west; the sky clears at dawn.
light: By night, deep blue darkness lit by the warm amber glow of the pillar of cloud and fire standing between Israel and Egypt; at dawn, cold pale grey-gold light rising from the east behind the mountains.
clothing: Israelites in undyed wool and linen tunics and striped cloaks of brown, ochre, madder red and indigo, with head cloths and sandals, carrying bundles; Egyptian charioteers in white linen kilts with leather and bronze scale corselets.
